title_or_hook: The walking-Will: 4-2-5 to Penny (5-1) spacing without changing personnel (full text)
summary: The PM run's W9 mechanic, now in full text: a 4-2-5 team gets into odd spacing (close the B-gaps) by 'walking' the Will and reducing the DL, reaching Penny (5-1) spacing without changing personnel. The Chiefs do it as much as anyone; their pressures translate because only the presentation changes. The clip shows the Chiefs' 'SAW' pressure: pinching the front, bringing Nickel (Sam) and Will off the edge. Coaching points: attack the RB in pass protection and attack receivers in the run game. Companion posts define the DB 'red line' (the line a receiver must stay on running a fade; the DB's job is to push him off it toward the sideline, and stacking into the boundary is the read) and a practice-field tip (use the goalie-box edge as the red line when a soccer field is superimposed). Personnel counts alone misread this defense; the 'SAW' pressure is a named, recognizable front for matchup reasoning. Single-source film read, CITED; no counts or frequencies; the clip itself was not viewed, only described in text.
